# IELTS band calculator

Canonical page: https://nepocore.com/tools/ielts-overall/

Add Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking band scores, divide by four, then round to the nearest whole or half band using IELTS scoring guidance. This calculation uses component bands, not raw correct-answer totals.

## How to use it

1. Choose your Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking bands from 0 to 9 in half-band steps.
2. Select Calculate overall band, or try one of the worked example buttons.
3. Compare Average before rounding with the overall result. An average ending in .25 rounds up to a half band; .75 rounds up to the next whole band.
4. Check the receiving institution’s individual section requirements separately. The overall number alone does not establish eligibility.

## Example

Listening 6.5 + Reading 6.5 + Writing 5.0 + Speaking 7.0 = 25.0. Divide by four to get 6.25, which rounds to overall 6.5. The Writing band remains 5.0.

## Limits and checks

This is an independent arithmetic tool, not an official score report or an affiliation with IELTS. Raw-score conversions for Reading and Listening are estimates in separate tools. Admission, visa and test-validity requirements must be checked with the recipient.

## Worked IELTS rounding examples



| Listening / Reading / Writing / Speaking | Average | Overall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5 / 6.5 / 5.0 / 7.0 | 6.25 | 6.5 |
| 6.5 / 6.5 / 5.5 / 6.0 | 6.125 | 6.0 |
| 8.0 / 8.0 / 7.5 / 7.5 | 7.75 | 8.0 |
| 7.5 / 7.0 / 6.5 / 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 |

## Overall band and section minimums answer different questions

Rounding changes the overall reported band; it does not raise a low Writing or Speaking score. If a programme asks for an overall score plus a minimum in every section, compare both conditions against its current published requirements.

Academic and General Training use the same overall averaging method. Their Reading raw-mark interpretations can differ. Use the appropriate raw-score tool when you have a practice mark out of 40, then treat the conversion as indicative rather than a promised official result.

## Task questions

### Does an average of 6.25 become 6.5?

Yes. IELTS rounds an average ending in .25 up to the next half band. An average of 6.125 rounds to 6.0 instead.

### Does 7.75 round to 8.0?

Yes. An average ending in .75 rounds up to the next whole band. Add all four components before applying the rounding rule.

### Do Academic and General Training use the same overall rule?

Yes. Both average the four component bands and round to the nearest whole or half band. Raw Reading conversions are a separate question.
